overview: Sri Bhadrakali Temple is one of the oldest and most revered temples dedicated to Goddess Bhadrakali in India. Located between Warangal and Hanamkonda in Telangana, it stands on the banks of the picturesque Bhadrakali Lake, surrounded by rocky hills and lush greenery. The temple is dedicated to Goddess Bhadrakali, a powerful form of Goddess Parvati symbolising courage, protection, prosperity and divine energy. The presiding deity is a magnificent single-stone (Ekashila) idol nearly 2.7 metres tall, depicted with eight arms holding divine weapons and a fierce expression. Originally built during the Chalukya dynasty (traditionally dated 625 AD by Pulakeshin II after his Vengi victory) and later patronised by the Kakatiyas — who worshipped her as their Kula Devatha (family deity) and built the adjoining Bhadrakali Lake — it is one of the most vibrant Shakti temples in South India, especially during Vasanta Navaratri, Sharannavaratri, Bonalu and Bathukamma. Stone and Goddess statues also dot the surrounding hills, making the entire hilltop a sacred landscape.
summary: Sri Bhadrakali Temple in Tadkamalla Village (Hanamkonda/Warangal), Telangana, is an ancient Shakti temple on the banks of Bhadrakali Lake, dedicated to Goddess Bhadrakali (a fierce form of Parvati). Built in 625 AD (traditionally by Chalukya King Pulakeshin II after his Vengi victory) and later patronised by the Kakatiyas as their Kula Devatha, it is famed for its ~2.7-metre Ekashila (single-stone) eight-armed idol. Regarded as one of the most sacred Shakti Peethas in Telangana, it draws lakhs of devotees during Vasanta Navaratri, Sharannavaratri, Bonalu and Bathukamma. Architecture blends Chalukyan and Kakatiya styles; surrounding hills have additional God/Goddess statues.

history.content: The temple has a history dating back to 625 AD and is believed to have been constructed by Chalukya King Pulakeshin II after his victory over the Vengi region. The king dedicated the temple to Goddess Bhadrakali as an expression of gratitude for her divine blessings and protection during his military campaign. It is one of the earliest examples of Chalukyan temple architecture in Telangana.
legends: Pulakeshin II built the temple as gratitude to Goddess Bhadrakali after his Vengi victory.
The temple is one of the earliest Chalukyan-era stone temples in the Telangana region.

history.content: During the Kakatiya dynasty the temple gained even greater prominence. The Kakatiya rulers — including Rudrama Devi — regarded Goddess Bhadrakali as their family deity (Kula Devatha) and contributed significantly to the temple's development; they also constructed the nearby Bhadrakali Lake, which served as an important water reservoir. The temple reflects a blend of Chalukyan and Kakatiya architectural styles. After the fall of the Kakatiya Empire, the temple gradually lost prominence but was revived in the mid-20th century through restoration efforts led by devotees and temple authorities.

history.content: The temple is administered by the Telangana state government's Department of Endowments, with the Executive Officer (EO) at eo.bhadrakali@endowments.telangana.gov.in. Mid-20th century restoration efforts revived the temple's prominence. The temple now attracts lakhs of devotees annually, especially during Vasanta Navaratri, Sharannavaratri, Bonalu and Bathukamma, and is a major Shakti Peetha in Telangana.

sthala_puranam: The temple is traditionally said to have been built in 625 AD by Chalukya King Pulakeshin II as a votive offering to Goddess Bhadrakali, thanking her for her protection and blessings during his victorious campaign over the Vengi region. The Kakatiya dynasty later embraced Goddess Bhadrakali as their Kula Devatha (family deity), elevating the shrine's stature and constructing the adjoining Bhadrakali Lake. The presiding Ekashila (single-stone) idol, with eight arms and a fierce expression, has been the focus of devotion for over 1,400 years. The temple's location on the lake's edge amid rocky hills is considered especially sacred.
religious_significance: Sri Bhadrakali Temple is regarded as one of the most sacred Shakti Peethas in Telangana. Devotees worship Goddess Bhadrakali as the embodiment of Shakti (divine feminine energy), believing she protects from evil, removes obstacles, and blesses with courage, prosperity and peace. As the Kula Devatha of the Kakatiya rulers, it holds immense historical and spiritual significance. The temple is especially popular among students, newly married couples, business owners and families seeking success and protection.
spiritual_significance: The 2.7-metre Ekashila idol represents both fierce power and compassionate motherhood. Devotees believe offerings of kumkum, coconuts, sarees, bangles, turmeric and special prayers fulfil sincere wishes. The serene Bhadrakali Lake setting — with sun reflecting off the water onto the temple during early morning and evening — enhances worship and meditation. The temple is also a major centre for Chandi Homam and Sri Chakra Pooja for those seeking protection and prosperity.

architecture: The temple showcases a beautiful blend of Chalukyan and Kakatiya architectural styles. Situated on a rocky hillock overlooking Bhadrakali Lake, it preserves several ancient stone pillars and structural elements near the sanctum despite renovations over the years. The main attraction is the magnificent Ekashila (single-stone) idol of Goddess Bhadrakali, about 2.7 metres tall, in a seated posture with eight arms holding divine weapons. The complex houses shrines to Lord Shiva, Lord Ganesha and other deities. Surrounding hills feature statues of various Gods and Goddesses; the entire setting amid gardens, the lake and rocky landscape is considered a sacred Shakti Kshetra.

darshan_and_tickets.general_darshan: General (Sarva) darshan is free of charge for all devotees.
darshan_and_tickets.special_darshan: Special Darshan (₹500, 7:00–8:00 PM) and paid seva tickets are available at the temple counter.
darshan_and_tickets.ticket_details: Tickets for Abhishekam, Kumkum Archana, Maha Mangala Harathi (₹200), Alankara Darshan (₹100), Special Darshan (₹500) and Ekantha Seva (₹100) can be purchased at the counter. Prasadam is sold at the ticket counter (high quality per Tripadvisor). Online booking is limited; obtain tickets at the temple. Separate queues and crowd management are arranged during Navaratri, Bonalu and other major festivals.

dress_code: Devotees are encouraged to wear traditional and modest clothing. Men generally wear dhoti, kurta or formal Indian attire; women are advised to wear sarees, salwar kameez or other decent traditional dresses. Shorts, sleeveless clothing and revealing outfits are discouraged. Footwear must be removed before entering, silence should be maintained in the sanctum, and photography may be restricted in certain areas. Telangana Tourism advises carrying water, light snacks, hats or umbrellas in summer.

accommodation.availability: The temple does not provide extensive on-campus accommodation. Devotees can find guest houses, lodges, budget hotels and premium accommodations in nearby Hanamkonda and Warangal city, within a few kilometres of the temple.
accommodation.booking_process: Reserve in advance through hotel booking websites or by contacting hotels directly — essential during Sharannavaratri, Bonalu and Bathukamma.
accommodation.price_range: Budget rooms ~₹600–₹1,200/night; standard hotels ~₹1,200–₹2,500/night; premium/business-class hotels ~₹2,500–₹5,000+/night. Tariffs rise during festival seasons.

best_time_to_visit: October to February for cool, pleasant weather. Best days: Monday–Thursday; best time 6:00–8:00 AM (or 5:00–7:00 PM when the sun reflects off the lake onto the temple). For a grand spiritual experience, visit during Sharannavaratri, Vasanta Navaratri, Bonalu or Bathukamma (very crowded).

travel.road: Approximately 150 km from Hyderabad, 3–4 hours via National Highway 163. TGSRTC operates frequent buses from Hyderabad, Karimnagar, Khammam, Nizamabad, Adilabad, Nalgonda and Siddipet; APSRTC connects from Vijayawada, Guntur, Visakhapatnam and Rajahmundry. Special buses run during Bonalu, Navaratri and Brahmotsavam. The temple is in the heart of the city and is easily reachable by auto-rickshaw at minimal cost.
travel.rail: Nearest station is Warangal Railway Station (~2–5 km), a major junction on the Delhi–Chennai main line, connected to Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Bengaluru, Nagpur, Delhi and Mumbai. Kazipet Junction (~10 km) is another option. Auto-rickshaws, taxis and city buses are available from both stations.
travel.air: Nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~160–170 km). Reach Warangal by taxi, TGSRTC airport bus, train or private vehicle. Warangal Airport is also operational for limited regional connectivity (per Wikipedia infobox).

introduction.en: Sri Bhadrakali Temple, between Warangal and Hanamkonda in Telangana, is one of India's oldest and most revered Bhadrakali temples, set on the banks of Bhadrakali Lake amid rocky hills. Dedicated to Goddess Bhadrakali, a powerful form of Parvati, it houses a magnificent single-stone idol about two point seven metres tall with eight arms. Built in 625 AD, traditionally by Chalukya King Pulakeshin II, and later patronised by the Kakatiyas as their family deity, it is a major Shakti pilgrimage centre, especially during Vasanta Navaratri, Sharannavaratri, Bonalu and Bathukamma.

history.en: The temple dates to 625 AD and is traditionally said to have been built by Chalukya King Pulakeshin II as a votive offering after his victory over the Vengi region. During the Kakatiya era it rose to prominence, as the Kakatiyas — including Rudrama Devi — worshipped Goddess Bhadrakali as their Kula Devatha and built the adjoining Bhadrakali Lake. The surrounding hills are dotted with statues of various Gods and Goddesses. After the Kakatiya decline the temple faded but was revived in the mid-twentieth century through restoration efforts.

travel_guide.en: Bhadrakali Temple is about 150 kilometres from Hyderabad, a three to four hour drive on National Highway 163, with frequent TGSRTC and APSRTC buses. The nearest railway station is Warangal, about two to five kilometres away on the Delhi-Chennai main line; Kazipet Junction is also nearby. The nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad, about 160 to 170 kilometres away. The temple is open from 5:30 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 8:30 PM; October to February is the best season. Buy prasadam early — it sells out and is high quality.

faq.question: Where is Sri Bhadrakali Temple located?
faq.answer: The temple is located in Tadkamalla Village, Hanamkonda, Warangal, Telangana – 506007, on the banks of Bhadrakali Lake between Warangal and Hanamkonda.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped in the temple?
faq.answer: The temple is dedicated to Goddess Bhadrakali, a powerful (fierce) form of Goddess Parvati. The presiding deity is a ~2.7-metre Ekashila (single-stone) eight-armed idol.

faq.question: What is Bhadrakali Temple famous for?
faq.answer: It is famous for its 2.7-metre-tall Ekashila (single-stone) idol of Goddess Bhadrakali, the stunning lakeside setting, and its historical association with the Kakatiya dynasty, who worshipped her as their Kula Devatha. The temple is dated to 625 AD (Chalukyan era).

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: The temple is open daily from 5:30 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 8:30 PM. Alankara Darshan 6:00–7:30 AM, Sarva Darshan 7:30 AM–12:00 PM, Maha Mangala Aarti 12:00–12:30 PM, Sarva Darshan 3:00–7:00 PM, Special Darshan 7:00–8:00 PM, Ekantha Seva 8:00–8:30 PM. Hours are extended during festivals.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No — general (Sarva) darshan is free. Paid options: Alankara Darshan ₹100, Maha Mangala Aarti ₹200, Special Darshan ₹500, Ekantha Seva ₹100. Seva tickets at the temple counter.

faq.question: Which is the biggest festival celebrated here?
faq.answer: Sharannavaratri and Vasanta Navaratri are the grandest festivals (nine days each), followed by Bonalu, Bathukamma, Bhadrakali Brahmotsavam, Shakambari Utsavam, Durga Ashtami, Ugadi, Maha Shivaratri, Karthika Masam and Deepavali.

faq.question: Is accommodation available near the temple?
faq.answer: Yes. Numerous hotels, lodges and guest houses are available in Hanamkonda and Warangal (the temple itself has limited on-campus accommodation). Haritha Hotel (Telangana Tourism), Hotel Suprabha, City Inn, Shreemaya and Ratna are popular options.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Bhadrakali Temple?
faq.answer: October to February for pleasant weather; early morning (6:00–8:00 AM) or evening (5:00–7:00 PM) for beautiful lake reflections. For a grand experience, visit during Sharannavaratri, Vasanta Navaratri, Bonalu or Bathukamma (very crowded).

faq.question: Who built the Bhadrakali Temple?
faq.answer: Traditionally built in 625 AD by Chalukya King Pulakeshin II as a votive offering after his Vengi victory. The Kakatiya dynasty (12th–14th c. CE) later worshipped Goddess Bhadrakali as their Kula Devatha and built the adjoining Bhadrakali Lake.

faq.question: What is the Ekashila idol?
faq.answer: The Ekashila (single-stone) idol of Goddess Bhadrakali is approximately 2.7 metres tall, depicted in a seated posture with eight arms holding divine weapons and a fierce expression. It is one of the largest single-stone Devi idols in Telangana and a major draw for devotees.
